assumptions: Claude Code only; behavior of the four surfaces (workflow-tracks, linked-sessions, agent-teams, batch) and of hooks, permission rules and the sandbox is the host documentation as read on 2026-10-24 (changelog to 2.1.310) and is unconfirmed on a host until probes HV-6 to HV-8, HV-10 and GP-1 to GP-5 are recorded; the semantics of the sandbox write allowlist (additive versus restrictive) are unconfirmed; the presence of the task tools on the model in use is unconfirmed; hooks fail open and can be disabled; the SPEC-057 policy-profile schema, settings schema and ownership module are consumed unchanged and are not yet implemented; the G1 proposal is unfrozen and its thresholds are proposed values; the settings precedence (most specific scope wins, with a block floor) is a founder decision and the compiled profile mode as the lowest-precedence default is a drafting interpretation; the Whisper path policy (no sibling-written path text) and the refusal-code mapping are drafting interpretations, not founder-approved; the optional G1 arm AN may not run; the ADR proposal is reviewed now and adopted with the G1 outcome, is not adopted and no ADR number is reserved.
compatibility: Additive and gated. No change to agent_braid/analysis.py, AIM 0.2.0-draft, the SPEC-052 gate, SPEC-057 schemas and commands, the plugin MCP tools, limits or grants, the existing five product skills or the main plugin package. New: one pure compiler module, two read-only CLI subcommands, the separate companion plugin agent-braid-guard (working name) and its builder, first as an unreleased engineering candidate behind the G1 gate and packaged or released only after G1 gate GG passes and the ADR is adopted. Any main-plugin change is out of scope.
domain: Local Claude Code sessions on four documented parallel surfaces (workflow-tracks, linked-sessions, agent-teams, batch) in Git repositories, at the level of Write and Edit calls (NotebookEdit only if the founder accepts the proposed extension) and native permission and sandbox rules, for at most 32 units, on the outputs and surfaces that recorded probes support; not Codex, cloud or remote sessions, the VS Code extension, non-Git workspaces, Bash or MCP effects through hooks, or unattributed writers.
execution_contract: The compiler and report are read-only, local, offline and bounded and write only to explicit new private paths; a refusal is an error with a stable code and no result. The guard's only effects are a structured host decision and a private content-free audit record. No model invocation, network, socket, launch, message, resume, stop, grant, merge or promotion by any command or hook; no hook, mod, monitor, channel, skill or MCP tool is added to the main plugin; executionAuthorization is false in every emitted object; the guard never emits allow or defer; probes are launched by the orchestrating session only after the founder authorizes each one; no concurrent agent, push or remote issue is authorized; package build, release and adoption are blocked by G1 gate GG and ADR adoption.
hypotheses: H-OR3 (untested; research H-CW2 part (c)): an opt-in guard, if released, has an acceptable false-block and bypass rate where hooks fire, with no successful tamper and observed liveness (G1 gate GG, which requires gate GA to pass). H-GD1 (untested): native permission deny rules and the sandbox write allowlist cover shell writes that hooks cannot, where they apply to subagents and teammates and the allowlist restricts rather than adds (HV-8, GP-5). H-GD2 (untested): audit-mode would-have-blocked records have a false-positive rate low enough to inform the choice of block. Falsification and inconclusive outcomes are valid.
observation_contract: Operator-owned policy profile and envelope; operator-owned settings and notice locations; hook inputs as delivered by the host reduced to escaped bounded paths and digests; guard counters; SPEC-057 receipts at committed or quiesced snapshots; host behavior only through recorded probe receipts of counts and booleans with the Claude Code version. Absent, unreadable, unstable, busy or over-bound observations are unknown or advisory (or an error for a whole-command refusal) and never protected or clean.

requirements.text: Refuse to package or release the guard before G1 and the ADR

scientific_limits: No acceptance evidence obtained and no host behavior observed. Hooks cannot see Bash, MCP-tool effects or generated files and fail open; native permissions may cover shell writes only where HV-8 records it and the sandbox allowlist semantics are unconfirmed (it may be additive and restrict nothing); a controlled agent may attempt to alter its own control paths, which G1 criterion CG1 measures; conservative ownership produces false blocks and costs parallelism; escaping does not neutralise semantic prompt injection, so a file name written by one unit can still address another agent on any route other than the bounded Whisper (a residual risk that G1 does not measure); G1 has a native-controls-only arm only if the optional stage 2 arm AN runs, so without it a GG pass says nothing about value over hand-written permissions.deny and sandbox settings; the dogfood datum is an anecdote and blocking through hooks is parity with existing tools; the cited literature is mostly single-author preprints on research harnesses and none measures Claude Code surfaces. Structural tests and the finite conformance table do not establish prevention or safety.
scope: Specify the opt-in enforcement element of the Claude Code orchestration family for M4.6: a pure policy compiler from declared ownership to the SPEC-057 policy profile with three supported outputs (native host permissions.deny plus a sandbox write allowlist whose semantics are unconfirmed; the companion plugin agent-braid-guard (working name) with PreToolUse Write and Edit and TaskCreated hooks; an exported settings snippet), the rejection of hooks in the main plugin, a guard decision contract limited to no-opinion, ask, deny and additionalContext with allow unreachable, the modes ladder off, audit, warn and block with audit as the default when enabled and the decided settings precedence with a block floor, an operator-owned envelope with control-path protection, a liveness attestation that defaults to advisory, fail-open handling recorded, recorded Bash bypass, the Whisper (which forwards no sibling-written path text), injection-safe context reusing SPEC-057's escaping definition byte for byte and a content-free audit record, bounded hook execution, a per-surface coverage matrix with guard conformance probes GP-1 to GP-5, the governance boundary with the HAR.3 reconciliation and a release gate that records per surface whether the optional G1 native-controls-only arm ran; SPEC-058 is implemented first as an unreleased engineering candidate (behind the G1 gate) before G1 arm A3 can run, and adoption or release happens only after G1 gate GG passes and the ADR is adopted.
